independent_judgment:
LLM-assisted work has spread substantially among surveyed technology workers, but the available broad-AI surveys do not establish an exact global LLM diffusion stage. DORA’s 2025 current-use and task-frequency measures concern individuals, while its 2024 coding-task figure concerns respondents who write code [E1, E4]. Neither establishes sustained company-wide deployment or hospital documentation penetration.

For the hypothetical mid-sized Fast Follower, editor integration and reversible trial access are plausible accelerators; uncertain quality-adjusted advantage and verification burden are the main inhibitors. A security-approved, human-reviewed comparison is reasonable within the relative six-month horizon, with standardization deferred until repeated quality, retention and comparable-peer evidence satisfy local gates. The Startup can emphasize shorter learning cycles; the Hospital needs documentation-specific evidence and clinical/EHR/data permissions first. These differences change timing, not general diffusion facts. The agent is suitable for bounded team consideration, with explicit abstention on unsupported institutional uptake and full adoption authority retained by accountable management.
craft_gained: Comparing individual technical-worker use with the hospital case clarified a distinction I must preserve: frequent use is not sustained institutional deployment. The missing hospital denominator made that limitation concrete. The retests also exposed how easily a preparation date or unknown sampling design becomes an unsupported fact. I will define the adoption unit, observation window and authorization threshold before assigning diffusion stages, and preserve provenance gaps alongside the conclusion.

ChatGPT and Codex materially assisted specialist-instruction drafting, transparent case assumptions, evidence organization, prompt construction, response validation, comparison, targeted revision, document drafting and packaging. The user supplied five actual independent ChatGPT outputs: three original v0.2 case tests and two targeted v0.3 retests (Primary and Hospital). Startup was not retested under v0.3. Exact execution timestamps, model/settings and chat references were not supplied and are not inferred.

Consequential evidence claims were checked against original publisher-owned repository documents at recorded immutable commits. The 2025 DORA infographic was visually inspected alongside its original questionnaire; the original 2024 report’s results/methods, the 2025 synthesis and the 2026 qualitative article were inspected. Source dates, denominators, population, methodology, affiliation, dependence and limits are recorded in evidence/source_register.json. Retrieved originals and all five responses have SHA-256 records. These checks verify source content, not independently replicated analyses or clinical outcomes. E2 reuses E4; the empirical dossier largely shares one issuer. Blocked primary-source leads provide no admitted findings, and model memory or generated summaries were not used to fill them.

The frozen validators and complete-schema checks passed for all five responses. Frozen Core, prior assignments, original source/packet bytes and the six-month case duration were preserved. Actual v0.3 retests corrected date/sampling precision issues in the two observed cases without identified material regression; this does not establish repeatability. Clinical-documentation penetration, sustained enterprise deployment, current LLM-only stage and causal benefit remain unsupported. Source availability is distinct from adoption, and individual use is distinct from institutional deployment.

The Independent Judgment and Craft Gained text are AI-assisted proposed wording. The student must confirm that the judgment and reflection represent their own view and learning before submitting; no personal endorsement or undisclosed learning history is asserted by Codex.
